ONE completely new, square, real photographic museum study of a lost sacred Raiatea royal maro ʻura. A respectful visual interpretation from old descriptions; it is NOT a photographed surviving Raiatea object.

Image references have separate, strict roles. Reference1 is a museum macro of the surviving Tahiti fragment: study ONLY its hand-knotted/plaited, irregular vegetal-fiber net support and rough old natural fibers. This is a different object, not a whole Raiatea belt; do not reproduce its fragment shape or faded brown palette. Reference2 is the approved treasure-series photograph: use ONLY its dark warm brown mottled textured background and soft upper-oblique dimensional lighting. No chest, gold, jewels or content from reference2.

SUBJECT: only ONE very long, narrow, old handmade feather belt of sacred royal regalia. About six metres of continuous belt, about fifteen centimetres wide. This must look like a genuinely long continuous handmade object, laid completely visible in MANY loose, unequal waves, with at least five gently curving passages across the arrangement and spacious rounded turns. Every part remains traceable along the single belt. Its two ends are visible and different, naturally worn/frayed vegetal-fiber ends, not precise rectangles. No modern neat strap, no buckle, no comb-shaped end caps, no clips, metal, fastener, reinforced bar or symmetrical tidy decorative terminations. No disconnected pieces or multiple belts. Constantly NARROW overall, with modest handworked edge variation. Not a broad cloak, cape, collar, skirt, fan, wreath, necklace or shaggy feather boa.

HANDMADE MATERIAL AND AGE ARE ESSENTIAL: dense real TINY red feathers individually tied in CLOSE ROWS onto a coarse vegetal-fiber net. Small feather shafts and branching fine barbs, physically overlapping rows, not large decorative petals or painted scales. Deep natural crimson/scarlet, softly varied rather than uniform manufactured red. The fibers are visible intermittently along both narrow edges, between a few gently worn feather areas, and at the two rough ends. Uneven hand-tied knots, slight asymmetric wear and a few naturally lifted feather tips. Keep it intact and sacred, not rotten debris. The dominant surface is densely RED featherwork. Some YELLOW feather areas occur at IRREGULAR positions and with UNEQUAL lengths and irregular boundaries: one short scattered yellow cluster, one somewhat longer partial-width patch, a separate broken yellow section elsewhere. NO regular yellow stripes, no evenly spaced transverse bands, no repeated modern red-yellow pattern. Feathers and cord must look physically natural under real light, not synthetic felt, printed textile, plastic, fur, painted or procedural texture.

ARRANGEMENT AND PHOTOGRAPHY: the entire long slender belt is loosely arranged in an organic series of several waves, five or more unequal passages, each bend broad enough not to look sharply folded or cut. The uneven wave pattern conveys much more physical length than a short tidy three-stroke S. Keep brown ground visible in the gaps. Comfortable margins around both ends and all turns; nothing cropped. Elevated oblique museum-photo camera reveals the fibers and layered feather relief. The dark warm brown textured ground and background are softly illuminated by the series' single soft upper-left oblique light. Dimensional gentle highlights on feather rows, clear but soft shadows below raised edges, deep natural shade between waves; rich depth, not flat front lighting. Entire object visible and convincing photographic material detail. Quiet respectful museum atmosphere with one sacred royal object only, no people, hands, mannequin, labels, text, border, watermark, shells, added ornaments, treasure chest or trophies. Fully opaque square photograph, no transparency.
